description: Groups hold what has to move together or fails together; anything that could fail on its own gets its own pull request, so one red update does not hold back the others.

packageRules.description: CI is the safety net: every update merges once it is green, majors included.
release-please only runs on main after a merge, so no check covers its update before it.
Give a new release three days to be flagged as malicious before it is proposed.
A runtime dependency's update reaches users, so it cuts a release.
Elixir is built for an OTP release, so the two move together.
Credo's plugins are built against its API, so they move with it.
The actions' small updates share the CI run that checks them.
The git hooks' tools are checked by one CI job, so their small updates share it.
The reference's update is test tooling; CI regenerates every reference with it. It stays apart from Python and uv, as a difference in its trees is a parser question.
Python and uv only run the reference script, so their small updates share a pull request.
